source.version: main snapshot reviewed 2026-07-21; no tagged release

capabilities.title: Treat divergent ideation as an explicit, higher-cost method
capabilities.adaptationNotes: Council must be enabled and the request must contain one of five explicit divergence phrases.

capabilities.title: Select materially different frames before generation
capabilities.adaptationNotes: Nexus uses three fixed, product-relevant frames: evidence auditor, inversion, and zero budget.

capabilities.title: Run frame branches independently in parallel
capabilities.adaptationNotes: The existing Council Promise.allSettled dispatch remains capped at three members and tells each member not to simulate the others.

capabilities.title: Use a separate critic to score options, cluster duplicates, and identify traps
capabilities.adaptationNotes: The optional merge draft pins one JANSKY call with novelty, viability, evidence, fit, clustering, trap, trade-off, shortlist, and first-step criteria.

capabilities.title: Make frames and method cost visible to the operator
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README call-count disclosure and output schema
capabilities.adaptationNotes: Tooltips disclose three calls plus one optional merge, and every divergent result shows its frame.

capabilities.title: Select from the larger upstream angle catalog
capabilities.reason: A fixed set of three Nexus-relevant frames is more predictable and avoids prompt/catalog overhead.

capabilities.title: Run the full roughly ten-call divergent and critic workflow
capabilities.reason: Nexus caps generation at three calls and makes the one-call critic optional to protect usage.

capabilities.title: Automatically activate divergent ideation for broad brainstorming requests
capabilities.reason: Normal brainstorming must remain one call unless the operator explicitly opts into Council divergence.

capabilities.title: Install and expose the upstream TypeScript CLI and library
capabilities.reason: The existing Nexus Council seam provides the selected behavior without another dependency, provider boundary, or runtime.
